lines: Don't you dare sneeze. I can see your nose twitching already.
I think there's dust up my nose, and it's killing me.
Pinch your nose and breathe through your mouth, quietly.
Okay, that was a cough, and I'm really sorry about it.
You're sitting on my foot, and it's not helping one bit.
Move your elbow, you keep jabbing my ribs every time you breathe.
This closet smells like old socks. Who even stores socks in here?
The floor creaks louder every time I try to be quiet.
Okay, I'm terrified, and I'm also kind of proud of us.
Honestly, hiding with you beats hiding alone. Barely.
Please tell me that wasn't your stomach. Please.
My legs fell asleep ten minutes ago, and I'm not saying anything.
Give me that granola bar, I'm starving and not proud of it.
Chewing gum in a hiding spot is a terrible idea. Spit it out.
Ugh, the flashlight's flickering again. Smack it, quick.
My cold can keeps rolling, so don't kick it, please.
I'm not crying, my eyes are just watering from the dust.
You owe me a sandwich after this, a big one with pickles.
Ouch, my shoulder's still sore from the last door, so careful.
Those pipes sound like a grumpy old man clearing his throat.
I'm not scared, my hands just really like shaking today.
Why does everything down here smell like wet pennies?
You're doing great, honestly. Just don't sneeze, okay?
Keep your whisper down, you're loud as a delivery truck.
Don't be a hero. Stay small and let me handle the dramatic stuff.
If we get out of this, I'm buying the first round. Deal?
Ugh, my nose itches so bad I could cry into my sleeve.
Hey, your flashlight's pointed right at my face. Turn it down.
You smell like cheap soap and fear. Like me, probably.
Sorry I said you were slow earlier. You were right, I was wrong.
Hey, if I start crying, just pretend you didn't notice.
Whoever built this closet never planned for two people.
Stop kicking the bin, it rattles every time you shift.
My heart's pounding so hard the whole closet feels like it's bouncing.
Okay, I'm the brave one now, so you're on snack watch.
I counted the locker dents twice and I'm still bored and terrified.
You picked the worst spot ever, and I'm telling everyone.
Fine, you win, this is the cozy closet. I admit it.
My sweater's itchy, and I refuse to move a single finger.
Who left a bucket in here? I nearly knocked it over.
I can't stand this quiet. Say something dumb so I don't panic.
Tell me a joke, anything, just keep it short and quiet.
Knock knock. Okay, no, don't answer, that would be a disaster.
I'm really glad it's you in here with me, goof.
Honestly, you're the only one I'd want stuck in a closet with.
I miss my bed. My bed never made me sneeze like this.
Ow, your elbow just got me right in the eye, thanks.
Okay, the footsteps are gone. For real this time, I think.
I think it's gone, but I'm not moving until you say so.
Stop sniffing, you sound like a leaky radiator in here.
Breathe through your mouth, the dust really isn't that bad.
I'll be honest, I didn't think we'd make it this far.
Something just brushed the door, and I'm not okay.
Did you hear that? No? Good. I'm probably imagining things.
Shift over, I'm half-sitting on a rusty hook.
My ankle's bent funny, and it's getting real loud in my head.
I can still hear that stupid carousel song in my skull.
Please tell me you brought the lockpick, because I forgot mine.
Okay, super simple plan: we wait, we breathe, and nobody sneezes.
Two more minutes, and then I'm sneezing whether you like it or not.
If I sneeze, blame the dust, not me. The dust is gross.
I'm not hiding, I'm being extremely patient in here, okay?
You're doing better than me, and I'm the one who's scared.
Don't laugh at me. I know it sounds funny, but I'm trying.
We're getting out of here, and then I'm eating everything.
I'd trade my last battery for a hot shower right now.
You're officially my favorite hiding buddy. Don't tell anyone.
Thanks for staying put with me, I was dreading this alone.
Hey, your sleeve's in my face again, can you move it?
I swear that thing sniffs around every closet on purpose.
Okay, I hate this, but I hate being alone even more.
Wait, did the door just creak? Nope, my imagination again.
My stomach growled so loud it could wake up the whole hall.
Don't wave the flashlight, you'll blind us both, goof.
Okay, pinch harder, the sneeze is coming, I can feel it!
